 Most recent Most popular Mainoo and Baleba published at 19:28 GMT 19:28 GMT 
 Man Utd v Roma (20:00GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter at Old Trafford 
 Finally Kobbie Mainoo and Carlos Baleba start together at the heart of Manchester United's midfield.
 This was always the plan but Baleba was injured when he completed his £70m move from Brighton and then Mainoo picked up a muscle issue just as his new team-mate made his debut from the substitutes' bench.
 Mainoo came off the bench at Chelsea on Saturday and is fit enough to start tonight.
 Michael Carrick needs the pair to hit it off.

 Barca bagging the goals published at 19:25 GMT 19:25 GMT 
 Barcelona v Aston Villa (20:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Barcelona will pose a huge goal threat to Aston Villa having scored 56 goals in 14 games this season, with former Leeds United forward Raphinha netting 15 and Lamine Yamal 10.
 "We haven't been talking about anyone in particular," Villa captain John McGinn said. They have world-class players in the starting XI and on the bench.
 "We respect the players who can hurt us, but we have our own players to cause damage to Barcelona."

 'Very exciting times for Villa fans' published at 19:22 GMT 19:22 GMT 
 Barcelona v Aston Villa (20:00 GMT) 
 Stephen Warnock 
Former Liverpool defender on BBC Radio 5 Live at Nou Camp 
 I think Aston Villa can mix it with the European elite. I think they have shown that over the last few times they have been in the Champions League. The games against PSG and Bayern Munich they more than competed - they won those games.
 They are a difficult team to play against and Unai Emery has got a new, younger 2.0 and I think he wants to show that off and I think he wants to show how far this team can go and it's very, very exciting times for Villa fans.

 Villa's rise helping McGinn realise childhood dreams published at 19:18 GMT 19:18 GMT 
 Barcelona v Aston Villa (20:00 GMT) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter 
 Image source, Getty Images John McGinn admits Aston Villa's rise to the Champions League has allowed him to fulfil his boyhood dreams.
 Before Tuesday's game in Barcelona, the Scotland international has revealed his ambition for Villa to continue to face the world's best clubs.
 Villa captain McGinn has only been to the Nou Camp once on holiday but is now ready to face World Cup winner Lamine Yamal on the pitch.
 "I used to go on holiday in Fuerteventura and Salou and I was here on a stadium tour the day Ricardo Quaresma signed for Barcelona," said the midfielder. "I've never been since but I'm excited to represent Aston Villa on the big stage.
 "I'm 32 years old and the trajectory of this club is allowing me to dream in the same way I did since I was nine, 10, 11.
 "What the club is trying to do now is make this journey and make it a yearly experience to compete with the best in England and Europe.
 "It's a pleasure to be on this journey with the supporters. I am sure they will enjoy today and tomorrow, but we will only enjoy the experience if we win three points."
 57 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Man Utd becoming 'painfully predictable' published at 19:15 GMT 19:15 GMT 
 Manchester United v Roma (20:00 GMT) 
 Pat Nevin 
Former Everton winger and presenter 
 Image source, Getty Images Another week and another Manchester United crisis is becoming painfully predictable.
 They haven't won in nine; they sit only two points off the bottom of the league; senior players have hit out at the hierarchy and the board is in the firing line.
 Against that backdrop, most felt that Michael Carrick would be gone by now.
 I wasn't so sure.
 With Roma, Aston Villa, Sporting and Liverpool coming up after Chelsea, the directors knew that their next choice could have had a disastrous start had they moved too quickly. No matter how good he is, that is a brutal introduction for a newbie with a struggling side.
 They probably reckoned it was best for Carrick to take the hits until after that run. If he turns it around in the meantime, then that works too because they get out of the danger zone. The only problem is that they could be staring up from the bottom of the Premier League by then.
 Pat Nevin writes weekly in the Football Extra newsletter. If you're outside the UK and would like to receive it, sign up here .

 Lively training session at Carrington published at 19:12 GMT 19:12 GMT 
 Manchester United v Roma (20:00 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Manchester United reporter 
 Michael Carrick watched over a lively open session of pre-match training at Carrington.
 Striker Bryan Mbeumo and midfielder Carlos Baleba were particularly vocal, with Argentina defender Lisandro Martinez also fully engaged despite his red card at Chelsea, which triggered such a negative reaction. 
 While there have been calls for Martinez to be dropped for the Roma game, Carrick was more philosophical.
 "Things happen in football," he said.
 "Sometimes you do things; you make a decision, you make mistakes. Sometimes it goes well for you."
 He also dismissed concerns both about Martinez's commitment, and that of his entire squad.
 "Perceptions are a funny thing," he said.
 "They can make things look all sorts of different ways. The dressing room is a good place.
 "I've said it before, I don't question the commitment of the players, to the club and to me and to each other. We need to play better. We can make better decisions. But commitment's not a thing at all."

 Ballon d'Or winner Kane can equal Ronaldo record published at 18:57 GMT 18:57 GMT 
 Atletico Madrid v Bayern Munich (20:00 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Tonight is Harry Kane's first Champions League game since winning the Ballon d'Or; a first opportunity to show Europe's elite why he won the prestigious award.
 Atletico Madrid fans were probably happy to see Kane beat Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe to the trophy but they'll hope their side can keep the England captain quiet tonight.
 After scoring 14 goals in 13 Champions League matches last season, Kane has four in three so far this campaign with a couple of assists to his name as well.
 Having scored in his last 10 appearances in the competitions, a goal tonight would see Kane equal the longest scoring streak in European Cup/UEFA Champions League history: 11 in a row by Cristiano Ronaldo for Real Madrid, between June 2017 and April 2018.
 64 17 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 18:54 GMT 18:54 GMT 
 Barcelona v Aston Villa (20:00 GMT) 
 Nick Mashiter 
BBC Sport football news reporter at the Nou Camp 
 It has been tipping it down in Barcelona for the last couple of hours and with the Nou Camp without a roof, there are going to be a lot of drenched supporters.
 Some Aston Villa fans already braved the weather with just under two hours before kick off as they huddled under umbrellas. 
 Unai Emery celebrates his 55th birthday today as he plots to take down Barca.
 His last Champions League game at the stadium was 'La Remontada' in 2017 when his Paris St Germain side collapsed in the last 16 to lose 6-1 - 6-5 on aggregate - having won the first leg 4-0.
 He brushed it off as just another game in his pre-match press conference on Monday but Aston Villa at the Nou Camp will not feel like a normal game for the 3,000 fans with tickets.
 63 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Carrick still in a job...Just published at 18:51 GMT 18:51 GMT 
 Manchester United v Roma (20:00 GMT) 
 Be honest, who thought Michael Carrick would still be in the job for tonight's match against Roma?
 Rumours around the Manchester United boss' future at Old Trafford have been circulating for several weeks now with United enduring a poor run of form which has seen them flirt with the relegation zone.
 Their last Champions League match - a 4-1 defeat by Como - intensified the scrutiny and they have not won a match since.
 It seems that if Carrick is to lose his job it may happen during the international break - that means he has two matches for things to start looking up.
 Tonight against Roma and Sunday against Aston Villa in the Premier League.
